text:
Maya (Support): FYI — Acme reported repeated 429s this morning around 09:12 UTC, but their project tile shows ~40% quota left. They believe dashboard underreports rolling-window usage.
Sam (Support): Posted their repro: high-concurrency batch job hitting /v1/generate at ~120 rps for ~90s, then bursts. They say 429s happen after ~45s into the burst.
Maya (Support): Here's the snippet customer sent for reproducing: 
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --d '{"model":"redwood-2-xl","input":"token test"}'
```
Jae (SRE): Can we get a request-id or x-rw-request header from their 429 responses? need those to trace. Also which project id they used?
Sam (Support): They provided two request-ids from the 429 responses: rq_01F6Z4A1 and rq_01F6Z4B2. Project id is proj-acme-01.
QuotaBot: Notice: org-level shared pool enabled for proj-acme-01. Remaining org tokens: 1.2M. Project-level remaining: 600k.
Jae (SRE): I pulled logs for rq_01F6Z4A1 — enforcement path shows RATE_LIMIT_TRIPPED at gateway layer (org_shard enforcement), response includes quota_bucket=org_shared_burst and window_start=1818654300.
Ollie (Platform): That aligns with a known ledger aggregation lag — project tiles render using the per-project ledger (near realtime), while the org shared pool enforcement checks a different rolling-window counter that can be updated slightly later. If the org shared pool is near depletion and many projects burst, you can get 429s even though the project tile looks ok.
Maya (Support): So the customer sees project tile with available tokens but is blocked by org pool? they were surprised because they thought project quota was independent.
Ollie (Platform): Correct — for org-shared pools the real enforcement is at org level. Dashboard per-project tile shows project-local quota only and doesn't include org-burst consumption. UX confusion. We should call this out more clearly.
Sam (Support): Customer asked for mitigation. What's the immediate workaround?
Jae (SRE): Short-term: ask them to move the bursty workload to a different project not sharing the org pool, or temporarily increase the org shared pool capacity. Also throttling their client to reduce sustained concurrency will avoid hitting the org rolling window.
Ollie (Platform): Long-term: we should 1) make project tiles include org-burst contribution or show an org-level banner when shared pool is enabled, and 2) fix the rolling-window aggregation to surface delays. I'll open INF-4521.
Maya (Support): I ran a quick repro in staging matching their burst profile and reproduced 429s when org pool consumption jumped. Attached minimal logs to the ticket.
Jae (SRE): Plan: canary deploy a fix that reads a single canonical rolling-window counter for both enforcement and dashboard within 2h, then monitor. If green, roll to prod.
Maya (Support): I told Acme the workaround and that we're rolling a fix to canary; they asked for ETA. I gave 3 hours.
Ollie (Platform): Created INF-4521 (P2) with replication steps and the sample request-ids. Will update here when canary is up.
Sam (Support): Added follow-up: update docs/quotas to clarify org-shared-pool vs project tiles.
Maya (Support): Closing loop with customer for now; will update when INF-4521 progresses. :thumbsup:
